sources.finding: Public LP4 mailbox parameter definitions and PHY host setup. Training loads fw-imem/fw-dmem arrays; no ARC algorithm located in inspected source. Only message definition/COPYING imported for tests.
Source-built LPDDR5 PMU exists. Its author states a clean-room provenance; this task has not independently certified that claim. No executable or source functions copied into the new LP4 components.

Public ST host PHY init and calculated skip-training delays. Normal training still loads external IMEM at STM32MP_DDR_FW_BASE. Older CSR layout and PHY insertion-delay assumptions do not establish T736 Type9 compatibility. Inspected only; no code imported.
Skip-training source warns it only supports a zero-board-delay model. No licensing basis for importing this file was established. Not imported or used to generate runtime settings.
16-bit access width, host mailbox offsets and common LP4 DMEM addresses corroborated. IMEM, DMEM private command data, PIE arrays and translated executable instructions were not imported.

corroborated_common_fields.scope: Offsets only; neither MR electrical settings nor full DMEM initialization is established by this component.

specific_lp5_incompatibilities: LP5 channel1 width/rank offsets 0x3f/0x40 collide with LP4 channel0 rank1 MR data; LP4 channel1 uses 0x57/0x58.
LP5 groups MR values by MR across four slices from 0x5a, while LP4 groups 12 MRs per channel/rank at 0x32/0x3e/0x65/0x71.
LP5 pmu_cal_rank_offset_get reads MR2 low nibble and returns zero for index >=12. Board-observed LP4 MR2=0x3f gives index 15, despite actual LP4 RL=36 at 1800 MHz.
LP5 pmu_cbt_delay_offset_lookup reads MR1 high nibble and returns zero for index >=12. Board-observed LP4 MR1=0xfc gives index 15, despite actual LP4 WL=18.
pmu_is_lpddr4 and pmu_is_lpddr5 inspect different LP5 MR19/MR20 fields and are not a mutually exclusive protocol selector.
pmu_rx_en_build_swizzle_map handles seven CA signals per slice; LPDDR4 has six CA signals and different command encoding.
LP5 eye/clock flows program WCK/RDQS paths and restore WCK delay registers; LPDDR4 uses DQS without a WCK interface.
The LP5 full sequence mask 0x125f contains bit6, reserved in the public LP4 1D sequence definition. Merely reusing the mask is invalid.
